text:
samir: quick ask — after the quant/kernel sweep last week, can we re-run the autoscale buffer analysis across regions? wanted concrete #s for concurrency targets per GPU and a recommended buffer% for Dedicated pools :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alice.wu: ran a short pass this morning against the bench harness. summary first: H100 gives ~18% better p50 token/sec on q4f16 vs A100, but p99 delta varies by seq len.

alice.wu: raw from the run (50k requests, mixed seq 32/128/512):
```
us-east (H100)  : p50=820 tok/s, p95=600 tok/s, p99=230 tok/s
eu-west (A100)  : p50=690 tok/s, p95=520 tok/s, p99=210 tok/s
ap-south (H100) : p50=780 tok/s, p95=580 tok/s, p99=240 tok/s
```

samir: thanks. do you have per-GPU concurrency headroom numbers (i.e., safe concurrent sessions per card for 99th-targeted SLOs)?

alice.wu: yes — using our continuous-batch model and limiting queuing to keep tail under 350ms for seq128:
- H100 (q4f16): 6 concurrent sessions per GPU (p99 ~340ms)
- A100 (q4f16): 5 concurrent sessions per GPU (p99 ~360ms)
- H100 (q8_0): 7 concurrent but token throughput drops ~8% vs q4f16

alice.wu: these assume KV cache warm and typical prefix reuse. cold-starts blow the numbers (reduce by ~30%).

priya: for Dedicated capacity planning I recommend using the lower bound (p99-safe) numbers and adding an autoscale buffer for regional surge. my call: provision for 80% of p50 capacity then autoscale buffer=25% for US/EU, 35% for APAC due to burstiness we measured.

samir: 25/35 seems reasonable but ops wants explicit node counts for the Q3 commit. can you translate those concurrency targets to GPUs for the expected 2000 concurrent sessions steady-state per region?

alice.wu: quick calc: use p99-safe concurrency per GPU (we pick conservative values: H100=6, A100=5)
- us-east (H100): base_gpus = ceil(2000 / 6) = 334 GPUs -> with 25% buffer = 418 GPUs
- eu-west (A100): base_gpus = ceil(2000 / 5) = 400 GPUs -> with 25% buffer = 500 GPUs
- ap-south (H100): base_gpus = ceil(2000 / 6) = 334 GPUs -> with 35% buffer = 450 GPUs

jorge: ops note: those GPU counts assume perfect packing and no tenant isolation. for Dedicated pools we need headroom for rolling upgrades and a warm pool (recommended 5% extra on top of buffer). also consider burst runway for N minutes.

priya: updated final ask: include warm_pool=5% and a 10-minute burst runway (measured as extra capacity to absorb 30% traffic spikes for 10m). we should encode autoscale policy to keep min=base_gpus, target_util=0.7, buffer_percent as above, and provision warm pool separately.

samir: can we show the autoscale config snippet to pass to infra?

alice.wu: sure, quick example (for us-east H100):
```
autoscale_policy:
  min_gpus: 334
  max_gpus: 1200
  target_utilization: 0.7
  buffer_percent: 25
  warm_pool_percent: 5
  burst_runway_minutes: 10
```

jorge: also add kernel-fallback rules: if H100 q4f16 queueing > 2m, route new requests to A100 q8 variant in eu-west as fallback. keeps availability good while quality delta is small.

priya: can we quantify cost delta? rough estimate for steady-state US pool: 418 H100 @ $X/hour vs 334 A100-equivalent. ops to fill exact $s, but expect ~20% higher infra cost for H100 footprint; savings come from lower latency and fewer GPUs for same concurrency.

samir: next steps: alice — produce a short one-pager with the numbers + CSV of per-region GPU counts and the bench harness config. priva/ops (priya/jorge) will review and sign off for Q3 commit by EOD Thursday.

autoscale-bot: automated note — load-tests scheduled in 2h for us-east cluster (id: lt-2026-09-14-02). will post results. :robot_face:

alice.wu: ack, will upload results to the bench run ticket and include raw latency histograms and prefix distribution.

samir: perfect. tagging @infra to make sure autoscale policy can be templated in terraform. thanks all :thumbsup:
